name: Shoot-day camera and sound media
one_line: Production-day camera originals, sound rolls, metadata, selects and handoff records kept together by the day they were captured.

deterministic: a call sheet, shooting schedule or slate log containing a shoot date and production or project identifier, alongside camera, sound or unit language
a camera-card, media-card or sound-roll manifest whose rows contain reel, card, clip or roll identifiers and whose surrounding files include a call sheet or production report
a handoff or checksum manifest explicitly naming camera originals, rushes, dailies, sound rolls or selects and linking them to a shoot date
needs_llm: a production-day folder whose only explicit signal is prose in a production report or email, with no standard call-sheet heading
deciding whether a set photograph documents a production day or is an ordinary personal/event capture when the image has no slate, crew, production or project context
mapping informal clip, reel and card naming conventions to one shoot day when the date is present only in neighboring documents
never_alone: a camera timestamp, EXIF record or video creation time alone; those establish capture evidence, not a production-day template
a folder named 'Day 1', 'rushes' or 'dailies' alone; these labels occur in personal recordings, exports and temporary working folders
a video or image extension alone; SOURCE_TYPES and extensions route extraction but do not establish a shoot or production context
a call sheet or calendar entry alone; it may describe a planned day for which no media exists and must not make unrelated files shoot-day media

grouping_reasons: one capture day linking its call sheet, camera cards, sound rolls, production report and rushes
one media handoff linking original media, checksums, metadata and selected exports
one production's repeated shoot days when a shared project identifier is directly established, while retaining each day's capture context

template.why: The creative schema is a placeholder with no inherited field rows, so this template recommends no destination dimensions yet. Its organizational distinction is procedural: call sheet → captured media → metadata and selection → handoff. A later schema pass may decide whether project, stage, artifact_type, event, capture_year or media_type are legal destination fields; this node must not mint them.

observations: filename contains CALL_SHEET and a date
document contains scene, crew-call and location sections
must_not_conclude: a creative project fact while the creative schema has no declared fields
that every file captured on the listed date belongs to this shoot

observations: sheet has clip names, card identifier, start time and checksum columns
nearby path or attachment names a production day
must_not_conclude: capture event or project without a corroborating production record
that checksum rows are themselves playable media

observations: video container metadata has a camera/reel/clip-shaped name
creation metadata is consistent with the date in a neighboring call sheet
must_not_conclude: production membership from filename syntax alone
that the file is a final deliverable rather than camera original or rush

observations: audio metadata identifies a broadcast-wave recording
roll number appears in a production sound report
must_not_conclude: the corresponding scene or project without a sound report or slate link
that a voice memo is a production sound roll

observations: labeled columns include date, scenes, camera cards, sound rolls and notes
rows cross-reference clip and roll identifiers
must_not_conclude: a folder path
that every listed clip was successfully recorded

observations: archive manifest contains proxy video, still thumbnails and a notes file
member names reference a shoot date and camera reels
must_not_conclude: that archive members are camera originals
that an archive is safe to extract or move without its manifest and fixity checks

observations: sidecar contains camera or editorial metadata fields
basename shares a clip stem with a media file
must_not_conclude: that the sidecar is independently meaningful without its media stem
a project or event from metadata keys alone

observations: filename says Selects and client review
video is a short assembled subset rather than a camera-card naming family
a handoff note links it to the shoot-day media
must_not_conclude: that it is a final deliverable or licensed master
that 'client' proves a career or commercial relationship without its agreement evidence

observations: document lists delivered media, checksum values, storage location and recipient
it references camera and sound roll identifiers
must_not_conclude: that listed media still exists at the stated destination
rights or licence facts; those belong to a later rights or career/legal treatment

observations: image has camera EXIF and a capture timestamp
frame shows a set or event but has no slate, call-sheet or production linkage
must_not_conclude: shoot-day media from EXIF or a set-like image alone
a production project or crew role

sensitivity_why: Production media can contain identifiable people, private locations, unreleased work and contact or delivery details. This is only the catalogue's potentially_sensitive flag; handling and protected-record policy belong to P7.
open_question: Should a production-day call sheet and its media be treated as one creative template when the work is personal or documentary, or should this template require an explicit project/production anchor and leave ordinary event captures to Photos? The current node requires the anchor and keeps the creative schema placeholder; Joseph must decide which future creative fields, if any, may become destination dimensions.
